STEPBible glosses wayyosef as 'and he repeated'; I render 'and Abraham added [and] took', since the idiom is 'he added to do (something)', i.e. 'again'. The verb carries no sense of repetition of a wife already taken in the narrative's own terms.

Isaac's age: Gen 21:5 has Abraham at 100 at Isaac's birth, so Abraham is 160 at the twins' birth and 175 at death (Gen 25:7), which makes the boys 15 at his death. That arithmetic is mine; it underlies the tradition in Rashi on 25:30 that Abraham died that day.

Five English versions split on 'tam' (plain / quiet / blameless) and on 'yode'a tsayid' (cunning hunter / skilful / expert bowman). 'Bowman' in BBE is an addition, not in the Hebrew. I kept 'knower of hunting' in the literal layer and 'complete/whole, unscheming' in the dramatic one; Rashi reads tam as 'not sharp at deceiving', Radak as 'without deceit', and the Targums as 'perfect' and 'studying'. I treat the study-house readings of the Targums as later interpretation.

'Tsayid be-fiv': literally 'game in his mouth'. The mouth is Isaac's (Onkelos, Rashbam, Ibn Ezra, Radak) or Esau's (Rashi's midrash, Pseudo-Jonathan: deceit in his mouth). Ramban gives both and prefers an idiom of constant presence. I follow the plain sense: Isaac's mouth. The KJV supplies a verb ('did eat') that the Hebrew lacks.

Pseudo-Jonathan's expansion (the day Abraham died, Esau's five sins) is not in the Hebrew and is not used in the dramatic layer. Rashi on 25:30 likewise says Abraham died that day and that the lentils are a mourner's meal; the plain text does not say so. I mention it in the commentary as tradition only.

[event:evt.gen_25.keturah_sons] Placing Keturah after Sarah's death (Abraham 137+) is an inference from the sequence of the text; some traditions (Pseudo-Jonathan, Rashi) identify Keturah with Hagar. The tradition does not change the date.

[event:evt.gen_25.ishmael_death] Ishmael's death at 137 (Abraham aged 223 from birth) falls after the events of Genesis 26-35 up to about Jacob's age 63; the narrator rounds up his account here. Dated by ages, not by the order of the text.
[event:evt.gen_25.twins_born] Anchoring on anchor.isaac_birth with 60 years reproduces anchor.jacob_birth, as expected. Abraham was then 160.

[event:evt.gen_25.birthright_sold] Date of the sale is unknown. Pseudo-Jonathan ties it to the day of Abraham's death (Jacob 15, with the lentil stew as mourners' food); the plain text says only that the boys had grown. Margin 8 years covers both.

Chapter-wide: Abraham and Sarah are reused from GEN.12. The corpus holds no ontology for Gen 16-24, so Hagar, Isaac, Ishmael, Rebekah, Machpelah, Mamre, Beer-lahai-roi and others are defined here, at their first mention in this chapter. If those chapters are ontologized later, those ids should be reused, not redefined.

No event covers 25:12-16 (the generations of Ishmael) or 25:19 (heading of Isaac's generations). Ishmael's sons and Hagar are first mentioned at 25:12-15, outside any event, so they are attached as MENTIONED to evt.gen_25.ishmael_death (25:17-18), the nearest Ishmael unit. Consider a chronologist event for the list.

[entity:person.israel] Jacob (named at 25:26, 'Jacob') is the existing person.israel (tipnr Israel@Gen.25.26-Rev, defined in GEN.37); no new entity. The Hebrew form here is Yaaqov; Israel is the later name (Gen 32). Not redefined.

[system:sys.divine_blessing_prosperity] Reused for God's blessing of Isaac (25:11): the existing system is 'the LORD makes someone prosper', and the content of the blessing is not stated here. A reviewer may prefer a separate sys.divine_blessing.

[entity:person.esau] Esau and Edom are one person (25:30 'therefore his name was called Edom'); Edom as a nation is not modelled as a separate entity yet.
[entity:person.keturah] Keturah is called a wife (ishah) at 25:1 but her sons are among those of the 'concubines' (25:6; 1 Chr 1:32 calls her a concubine). The state is coded WIFE with this caveat.
[entity:group.asshurim] Asshurim (25:3) is a descendant tribe of Dedan, not the Assyrians; defined without tipnr_id and kept separate from loc.assyria.
[entity:loc.land_of_the_east] 'Land of the east' (eretz qedem, 25:6) is a vague region, not a point; no coordinates and no registry entry.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.keturah_sons] No place stated for the marriage and births; left out rather than assumed.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.gifts_sendoff] No place stated; Abraham's residence is not restated. The destination (land of the east) is a state, not the place of the event.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.abraham_death] Place not stated in 25:7-8; left empty.

[event_links:evt.gen_25.ishmael_death] Place of death not stated. 25:18 gives the region his sons settled; it is recorded as the sons' dwelling state, not an event place. The last clause of v18 ('he fell in the presence of his brothers') is read as Ishmael's death/settlement, debated; not modelled as a separate act.

[event_links:evt.gen_25.isaac_marries] Place left out: the marriage is told in Gen 24 and not restated here. The chronologist dates it 40 years into Isaac's life; the event sits after the narrative order of this chapter.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.prayer_conception] Place not restated; one might carry over Beer-lahai-roi from 25:11, but that verse is later in time (after Abraham's death), so it is not assumed.

[event_links:evt.gen_25.twins_struggle] 'She went to inquire of the LORD': the place (an altar, a prophet, a shrine) is unspecified; none given. The twins are PRESENT (in the womb); modelled as two persons already.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.twins_born] Isaac is MENTIONED only (his age is given at v26); the text does not place him at the birth.
[event_links:evt.gen_25.boys_grow] Place is the family encampment ('tents'), not named.

[component:comp.sons_of_ishmael.dwelling.1] State inferred from 25:18: they settled from Havilah to Shur; the region is coded as a value, not a single place. The site of Havilah and Shur in this verse is debated.
[component:comp.esau.birthright.1] Inferred: Esau holds the birthright as firstborn from his birth (25:25) until he sells it (25:33). The text names the birthright only in the sale scene.
[component:comp.rebekah.fertility.1] Barrenness is stated at 25:21 ('she was barren') but belongs to the whole period since the marriage (25:20); opened at 25:21, the first verse that says it.

[system:sys.divine_blessing_prosperity] Reused for God's blessing of Isaac (25:11): the existing system is 'the LORD makes someone prosper', and the content of the blessing is not stated here. A reviewer may prefer a separate sys.divine_blessing.

[system:sys.birthright_transfer] Defined here: the sale of the firstborn's rights is not the same as sys.sale_of_person (Gen 37). Parallels cited (Nuzi) are about firstborn inheritance shares and are debated for this passage.
[system:sys.binding_oath] Defined here, since sys.oath_by_yhwh is an oath by the living LORD and 25:33 does not say by whom Esau swears.
[system:sys.petition_prayer] Defined here as the general practice (Isaac entreats the LORD for Rebekah), because no prayer system exists yet in the corpus.
[system:sys.oracle_inquiry] Defined here: Rebekah inquiring of the LORD and receiving an oracle (25:22-23). It is distinct from sys.divine_word_to_prophet because no prophet is named.

[system:sys.burial_in_family_tomb] Defined here; the existing sys.mourning_rites covers mourning, not burial. The 'gathered to his people' formula (25:8) is treated as part of the death account, not as the burial itself.

[system:sys.inheritance_of_estate] Defined here: inter vivos gifts to the concubines' sons and the whole estate to the heir (25:5-6). Terminology of the 'gifts' is debated; the mechanics are those the text implies.
[entity:substance.lentil_stew] Included because the plot turns on it (25:29-34); the 'red stuff' (adom) is the Edom pun.
